_meta.purpose: Synthetic dataset for the buildd product demo video. All names, ids, repos, people and numbers are fictional.

conventions.keys: Every entity has a `key` (e.g. 'T3', 'w3'); cross-references use keys. The seed script mints UUIDs and maps keys → ids.
conventions.idShort: Tasks/missions carry `_idShort`: force the first 8 hex chars of the minted UUID to this so branch names (`buildd/<id8>-<slug>`) match.
conventions.fieldNames: Drizzle property names (camelCase) from packages/core/db/schema.ts. `table` is the SQL table name.
conventions.underscoreFields: Fields starting with `_` are NOT columns — notes, end-state targets, or display hints.
conventions.timeline: t = seconds from mission creation. Rows in entity lists are the INITIAL state; the timeline mutates them. `_statusAtEnd`/`_final` give the target end state for a static (non-replay) seed.
conventions.relativeTimes: '-3d' style values are relative to demo start.

artifacts.title: FX rate providers compared
artifacts.content:
## Recommendation
Primary: Provider B (hourly mid-market, flat monthly). Fallback: central-bank daily reference rates.

## Why
- A updates every minute but bills per call; our read pattern is bursty around invoice runs.
- B's hourly cadence is well inside a 15-minute cache + snapshot-at-issue design.
- C had no documented behaviour during outages.

## What breaks when rates are down
Nothing customer-facing if we snapshot the rate on the invoice at issue time. Checkout reads the snapshot, not a live rate.
artifacts._column_note: artifactKey -> artifacts.key (unique per workspace). 'key' here is the dataset ref.

artifacts.title: Decision: round converted amounts per line
artifacts.content:
Converted invoices round **each line** to the customer currency's minor unit. The total is the sum of rounded lines, so it always equals what Stripe charges. The ledger export carries a `rounding_delta` column so finance can reconcile to base currency.

_Decided by Maya Okafor via the mission feed._

missionNotes.title: Plan: 3 phases, 12 tasks
missionNotes.body:
**Foundations** (5, parallel): schema, FX service, currency picker, formatMoney, provider research.
**Currency through the product** (5): API, invoice render, checkout, export, receipts.
**Prove it** (2): EUR end-to-end test, admin guide.

Rates are snapshotted at invoice issue so checkout never waits on a live rate.

missionNotes.title: Round per line, or only the total?
missionNotes.body: Converting a multi-line invoice, rounding each line to cents can differ from rounding the total by up to one minor unit per line. Per line: the total equals exactly what Stripe charges the card. Total only: matches the base-currency ledger, but the card charge can be off by a cent or two. Which should be the source of truth?

missionNotes.title: Per line
missionNotes.body: Per line. The card charge is what customers see. Put the delta in the export so finance can reconcile.

memories.title: Converted amounts round per line, never on the total
memories.content: Line-level rounding keeps the invoice total equal to the card charge. Reconcile to base currency via export.rounding_delta.

memories.title: Invoice PDF snapshots are locale-sensitive
memories.content: Snapshot tests run under several locales. Format through formatMoney(amount, currency, locale) — never toLocaleString() with the process default.

memories.title: Snapshot the FX rate at invoice issue
memories.content: Store fx_rate_snapshot on the invoice. Anything downstream (checkout, receipt, export) reads the snapshot so a provider outage can't change what a customer owes.

memories.title: Dark mode tokens live in one CSS layer
memories.content: All color tokens come from styles/tokens.css; components never hardcode hex. Portal and admin share the layer.

memories.title: PDF render time was dominated by font loading
memories.content: Embedding a subset font and reusing one renderer instance per worker process removed most of the per-invoice cost.
